title: Job-change interpretation
about: A job change is the best reason to get back in touch, but most "changes" in an export are noise: a reworded title, or a promotion inside a function that never buys from you. Code notices that a title changed. Jev decides what the change means. Code decides what to do about it.

rules: Skip contacts on the suppression list.
Send text that looks like an instruction to the model to a person.
Same title and company after normalising case and spacing: no change, ignore.
0_filter_and_cache.cache: Answer store. Fingerprint = questions + model + state; a stored answer is reused with no Jev call.

change_type.instructions: Compare the role in `previous` with the role in `current`. What kind of change is this?

criteria.moved_up: A step up in seniority, scope or responsibility
criteria.moved_sideways: A different job at a similar level of seniority
criteria.same_job_reworded: The same job and employer written differently, such as an abbreviation being spelled out or a team name added
criteria.moved_down_or_unclear: A step down, a gap in employment, or not enough information to say

new_budget_owner.instructions: Does the role in `current` own a budget for `what_we_sell` that the role in `previous` did not?

criteria.true: The new role runs the function that would buy this, and the old role did not
criteria.false: Buying power for this is unchanged, lower, or was already there before

current_role_buys.instructions: Is the role in `current` one whose holder decides whether to buy `what_we_sell`?

criteria.true: They run sales, revenue, growth or the whole company, so they would own this decision
criteria.false: Their function does not buy this, even if the role is senior

rules: Account is a customer or has an open opportunity: route to the account owner, not outreach.
A fit score below min_fit, from playbook 01 or 06: ignore. A missing fit score does not filter.
Otherwise reach out; new_budget_owner at or above its cutoff marks "just gained the budget".

3_write.ask: Write a two-sentence LinkedIn message to this person about their new role. End with one easy question about the role.

actions.reach_out: Draft waits for approval; a person sends it.

4_act.ledger: Every record is logged with its input, answers, facts, the rule that decided, and the outcome.

lessons: The first version asked one broad question, "is this move a good reason to get in touch now?". It could barely tell the cases apart: 73%, 42%, 64% and 44%. Replacing it with the narrow "does the current role buy this?" separated them: 77%, 34%, 73% and 14%. When a question gives mushy probabilities, split it.
The old and new roles go into the state together as named fields, so Jev judges the relationship between them.
Use new_budget_owner to order the reach-out list: someone who just gained the budget is a warmer conversation.
limits: Titles are all there is to go on. "Director" can mean a team of 2 or 200.
Senior but in the wrong function is the case to watch. Check the cutoffs against people you know.
